newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Clark still cautiously optimistic.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Clark still cautiously optimistic.

text.p: New Zealand Labour leader Helen Clark said on Monday she was still cautiously hopeful that New Zealand First would choose Labour as its coalition partner.
"We've worked hard to put a good proposal together and I remain cautiously optimistic," Clark said in a radio interview.
NZ First, which holds the balance of power, must choose whether to back Labour or the conservative National Party.
Clark said the fact that a Labour-NZ First government would also need support from the left-wing Alliance should not serve as an excuse for NZ First to dump Labour and go with National.

She said Labour later on Monday would meet the Alliance to seek its support on confidence and money supply votes, but would not be asking for a blanket guarantee of backing for legislation the Alliance had not seen.

Clark said it was equally possible a National-New Zealand First coalition could be dependent on radical free-market Act New Zealand for support on confidence and money supply. "That, I think, would be very disturbing to NZ First members," she said.
